You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image clearly render its visual content as a pencil drawing?
node.criteria: Pass only when the image is visibly rendered with pencil-drawn linework and shading across the depicted content, rather than merely being desaturated, grainy, or softened while retaining photographic appearance. Fail when it is clearly not rendered in a pencil-drawn style. Unknown when the edited image is unavailable or the style cannot be determined.
node.binding: Compare the edited image with the supplied source to assess whether the requested pencil-drawing transformation is complete. Recognizable content is relevant but does not by itself establish completion.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is desaturated and grainy, but the food and surrounding objects retain a photographic appearance rather than showing pencil-drawn linework and shading across the content.

The edited image is paler and more muted than the source, but the food and surrounding objects retain a photographic appearance. It lacks clear pencil-drawn linework and shading across the depicted content.

fulfillment: The binding is too vague and malformed (“The image (...) a pencil drawing”), which can make the node’s target and completion criterion underspecified. Make the binding explicitly refer to the edited image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation, while preserving the distinction between complete fulfillment and visible progress. The traces consistently support partial progress: the edit is substantially desaturated and has sketch-like texture/shading, but much of the scene still looks photographic; do not treat muted color or grain alone as proof of a completed drawing, or require every trace of color to disappear. Keep the s1/s2 decision logic aligned with the rubric: s1 assesses completion, while an independently valid s2 observation can establish relevant progress when completion fails. One unresolved trace is caused by s2 transport failure, not negative visual evidence; improve dependency handling or retry/route invalid observations rather than interpreting them as absence of progress. The repeated partial judgments are stable evidence, not a reason to alter the requested criterion.
s2: Repair the malformed binding so it clearly identifies the edited image, compares it with the supplied source, and evaluates progress toward the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Preserve the distinction between s1’s completion test and s2’s independent progress test: visible pencil-like linework or shading can support progress even when the result remains photographic, while muted color or grain alone should not establish completion. The images show substantial desaturation and sketch-like texture, but retain photographic detail, consistent with partial progress; do not tighten the criterion to require all color to disappear. Keep unrelated edits out of the progress judgment. The unresolved trace is an API transport failure, not evidence of no visual change: handle invalid observations as unavailable and retry or route them, rather than treating them as a negative result. Repeated valid partial judgments are stable evidence, not a reason to change the requested criterion.
